concept_html:
Every pandas column has a dtype. The wrong dtype gives wrong answers without an error: IDs that lose leading zeros, counts that turn into floats, text that sorts as numbers.

Three facts about pandas 3.0:

  • Text columns default to the str dtype. pd.Series(["a", None]).dtype prints str, not object. Missing values in it are NaN. Only strings are allowed, so a stray integer no longer hides in a text column.
  • A missing value turns an integer column into float64, unless you ask for a nullable dtype. pd.Series([1, None]) is float64. pd.Series([1, None], dtype="Int64") keeps integers and shows the gap as <NA>.
  • Setting a value that does not fit raises. Assigning 1.5 into an int64 Series raises TypeError instead of silently upcasting the column. (Assigning NaN still upcasts to float64.)

The capital letter matters. int64 is NumPy's integer with no missing values. Int64, Float64 and boolean are pandas nullable dtypes that hold pd.NA.

Set dtypes where data enters, not later:

df = pd.read_csv(
    path,
    dtype={"respondent_id": "str", "postcode": "str", "household_size": "Int64"},
)

Without the dtype map, read_csv reads a postcode such as 01234 as the number 1234.0 once any row is blank. With it, "01234" stays a string.

Check the result with df.dtypes right after loading. df.convert_dtypes() switches every column to the nullable equivalents in one call, useful for exploration. An explicit map is better in pipelines, because it fails loudly when the source changes.

lines: import pandas as pd
PANEL_DTYPES: dict[str, str] = {
"respondent_id": "str",
"household_size": "Int64",
}
def read_panel(path: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
"""Read one panel wave with explicit dtypes."""
return pd.read_csv(path, dtype=PANEL_DTYPES)

exercises.solution:
import io

import pandas as pd

PANEL_DTYPES: dict[str, str] = {"respondent_id": "str", "household_size": "Int64"}


def read_panel(text: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Read panel CSV text with explicit dtypes.

    Args:
        text: CSV content with respondent_id and household_size.

    Returns:
        A frame with str IDs and nullable integer counts.
    """
    return pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(text), dtype=PANEL_DTYPES)

title: Dtypes in pandas 3, nullable and string
why_html:
A panel file stores respondent IDs such as 00731. One wave has a blank ID row, so read_csv infers float64 and the ID becomes 731.0. The join to the previous wave, where IDs were read as text, matches nothing. The longitudinal report shows 0% retention for a panel that kept 82% of its members.

dtype={"respondent_id": "str"} at load time keeps 00731 as written in every wave.
